title: CRLR/256/2010 of BACHAN SINGH AND ORS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.256 of 2010
Bachan Singh & Ors. .Ö Revisionists
Versus
State of Uttarakhand Ö.. Respondent
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for the revisionists
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Deputy A.G. along with Ms. Shivangi Gangwar, Brief
Holder for the State

JUDGMENT
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
 This criminal revision is directed against the
judgment and order dated 21.12.2009 passed by
Judicial Magistrate, Purola, District Uttarkashi in
Criminal Case No.272/2008 as well as the judgment
and order dated 26.11.2010 passed by Sessions Judge,
Uttarkashi in Criminal Appeal No.04/2010, whereby
said courts have convicted the revisionists under
Section 323 of The Indian Penal Code, 1860 and has
sentenced them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for
a period of one month along with a fine of Rs.100/-.
Accused/revisionists have been further convicted
under Section 504 of IPC and have been sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two
months along with a fine of Rs.150/-.
2. Prosecution story, in brief, is that
complainant moved an application u/s 156(3) of
Cr.P.C. before the Judicial Magistrate, Purola stating
that on 22.5.2008 the complainant was tying her cattle
meanwhile the accused/revisionists came there and
began to open the rope of the cattle.

2
Accused/revisionists cut tail of one animal with sickle
(sharp edged weapon). When the complainant tried to
stop them, accused/revisionist Bachan Singh
assaulted her with kicks and fists. Other
accused/revisionists also committed Marpeet with the
complainant and used abusive language. While going,
the accused/revisionists threatened her for dire
consequences. On the application, F.I.R. was registered
against the accused/revisionists at P.S. Purola. Matter
was investigated. On completion of investigation,
charge-sheet was filed against the accused/revisionists
under Sections 323, 504, 506 of IPC. On 07.02.2009,
charge was framed against the accused/revisionists
under 323, 504, 506 of IPC, to which they pleaded not
guilty and claimed to be tried. On denial, trial begun.
In order to prove its case, prosecution got examined as
many as five prosecution witnesses viz. PW1 Smt.
Hema Devi, complainant, PW2 Urmila, eyewitness and
daughter-in-law of complainant, PW3 Ameen Singh,
eyewitness and son of complainant PW4 Smt. Shishma,
PW5 Khajan Singh, Medical Officer. After closure of
prosecution evidence, statement of the
accused/revisionists were recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P.C.
in which they denied the allegations levelled against
they. However, they did not adduce any evidence in
defence. After hearing the parties and on perusal of
evidence, trial court convicted and sentenced the
revisionists/accused as above. Feeling aggrieved,
revisionists/accused preferred appeal before the
Sessions Judge, Uttarkashi, which also got dismissed
by the judgment and order impugned.

3
4. Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, learned counsel for the
revisionists would confine his argument qua the
quantum of sentence only. He would submit that the
incident relates to the year 2008 and more than 10
years have passed till date. Since then the revisionists
are facing mental agony due to the pendency of the
criminal case against them. He would also submit that
the maximum sentence awarded to the revisionists is
two months u/s 504 of IPC, and out of the same, they
have actually undergone incarceration for more than
one month. He, thus, prayed that the sentence
awarded to the revisionists may be reduced to the
period already undergone by them.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the entire record.
6. Having considering the submissions of
learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the
record, I do not find any illegality or perversity in the
impugned judgment and orders passed by the courts
below. The trial court as well as the appellate court has
rightly convicted the revisionists under the aforesaid
sections. The conviction of the revisionist is, therefore,
affirmed.
7. Insofar as the quantum of sentence of
imprisonment is concerned, the revisionists have
already served the period of one month in jail out of
total two monthís imprisonment. Furthermore, the
incident is of the year 2008 and no useful purpose
would be served by sending the revisionists behind the
bars after a period of 11 years. In such circumstances,

4
it would be just and expedient to reduce the sentence
qua imprisonment of the revisionists to the period
already undergone by them, without disturbing the
sentence of fine.
8. Accordingly, criminal revision is partly
allowed while maintaining the conviction of the
petitioner under Section 323 and 504 of IPC. However,
for the reasons stated above, sentence of imprisonment
is modified to the extent that the revisionists are
sentenced for the period of sentence already undergone
by them alongwith fine as directed by the courts
below.
9. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the
trial court for ensuring compliance. Lower court record
be also sent back.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
07.03.2019
Rajni
